candidates.name: Carlos D. Shelden
candidates.short_description: Upper Peninsula soldier, businessman, and congressman.
candidates.biography: Carlos D. Shelden moved to Houghton County as a child, served as a Michigan infantry captain through the Civil War, and built businesses in mining, machinery, real estate, and steamboats. He later served in the Michigan Legislature and represented the Upper Peninsula in Congress.
candidates.why_interesting: His life followed the Upper Peninsula from frontier industry through Civil War service and into national politics.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Carlos D. Shelden.
image.creator: Evening News Association (Detroit, MI), publisher.
image.attribution: Evening News Association (Detroit, MI), publisher. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Jay Abel Hubbell
candidates.short_description: First congressman from Michigan's old Ninth District.
candidates.biography: Jay Abel Hubbell was a lawyer, prosecutor, and judge whose public career grew alongside the mining communities of the Upper Peninsula. He served five terms in the U.S. House and became the first representative elected from Michigan's Ninth Congressional District.
candidates.why_interesting: He helped give the rapidly developing Copper Country a durable voice in Washington.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Jay Abel Hubbell.
image.creator: Mathew Benjamin Brady / Levin Corbin Handy
image.attribution: Mathew Benjamin Brady / Levin Corbin Handy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: William D. Cochran
candidates.short_description: Michigan football captain and Federal Reserve director.
candidates.biography: William D. Cochran played guard and tackle for Michigan from 1913 through 1915, earning all-Western recognition and captaining the 1915 Wolverines. Back in the Upper Peninsula, he ran a freight line and later spent years directing the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis.
candidates.why_interesting: His résumé jumps from the football field to trucking and central banking.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of William D. Cochran.
image.creator: Unknown photographer
image.attribution: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: H. Olin Young
candidates.short_description: Upper Peninsula lawyer, prosecutor, and congressman.
candidates.biography: H. Olin Young built a legal career in Ishpeming, served as Marquette County prosecutor, and represented Michigan's Twelfth District in Congress during the early twentieth century. His work linked local law and mining-country politics with federal service.
candidates.why_interesting: For years he carried the concerns of the western Upper Peninsula from Ishpeming to Washington.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of H. Olin Young.
image.creator: Harris & Ewing
image.attribution: Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: John W. Stone
candidates.short_description: Michigan judge who served in Congress and on the state Supreme Court.
candidates.biography: John W. Stone began as an Allegan County clerk and prosecutor before becoming a circuit judge and two-term U.S. representative. After serving as U.S. attorney for western Michigan, he returned to the bench and spent his final years as a justice of the Michigan Supreme Court.
candidates.why_interesting: His career touched nearly every level of Michigan's legal system over six decades.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of John W. Stone.
image.creator: “The U.S. House of Representatives - Portraits of Congressmen” (detail), Harper’s Weekly 1891, Collection of U.S. House of Representatives
image.attribution: “The U.S. House of Representatives - Portraits of Congressmen” (detail), Harper’s Weekly 1891, Collection of U.S. House of Representatives · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Fred Burke
candidates.short_description: Prohibition-era gunman and St. Valentine's Day Massacre suspect.
candidates.biography: Fred “Killer” Burke was an armed robber and contract killer whose criminal career crossed several Midwestern states during Prohibition. Investigators considered him a leading suspect in Chicago's 1929 St. Valentine's Day Massacre.
candidates.why_interesting: One of the era's most wanted gunmen ended his story in a Marquette prison and cemetery.

candidates.name: Carroll Watson Rankin
candidates.short_description: Marquette author of the children's classic Dandelion Cottage.
candidates.biography: Caroline Clement Watson Rankin wrote under the name Carroll Watson Rankin and began reporting for Marquette's Daily Mining Journal as a teenager. Her novels, especially Dandelion Cottage, turned Upper Peninsula settings and childhood adventures into enduring regional literature.
candidates.why_interesting: Her best-known story made a real Marquette cottage part of Michigan literary history.

candidates.name: Frederick Eis
candidates.short_description: Catholic bishop who led the Upper Peninsula diocese for 23 years.
candidates.biography: Frederick Eis was a German-born Catholic prelate who served as bishop of the Diocese of Sault Sainte Marie-Marquette from 1899 until retiring in 1922. His long tenure covered remote parishes and mining communities across Michigan's Upper Peninsula.
candidates.why_interesting: He led one of Michigan's most geographically demanding dioceses through a generation of change.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Frederick Eis.
image.creator: Unknown photographer
image.attribution: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Robert P. Griffin
candidates.short_description: Michigan senator who broke with Nixon during Watergate.
candidates.biography: Robert P. Griffin represented Michigan in the U.S. House and Senate before serving on the Michigan Supreme Court. A Senate deputy minority leader, he publicly urged fellow Republican President Richard Nixon to resign as the Watergate crisis deepened.
candidates.why_interesting: His call for Nixon to step down placed a Michigan senator inside a decisive Watergate moment.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Robert P. Griffin.
image.creator: United States Senate Historical Office
image.attribution: United States Senate Historical Office · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Demas T. Craw
candidates.short_description: Medal of Honor recipient killed during the North Africa campaign.
candidates.biography: Demas T. Craw was a U.S. Army Air Forces officer killed in 1942 while volunteering for a dangerous mission during the Allied landings in North Africa. He received the Medal of Honor for valor outside aerial combat, an unusual distinction for an Army airman.
candidates.why_interesting: His final mission made him one of the first Army Air Forces Medal of Honor recipients in the European-Mediterranean theater.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Demas T. Craw.
image.creator: United States Army Air Corps
image.attribution: United States Army Air Corps · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Perry Greeley Holden
candidates.short_description: America's first professor of agronomy and a farm-extension pioneer.
candidates.biography: Perry Greeley Holden became the first professor of agronomy in the United States and later led agricultural extension work at Iowa State. Known as the “corn evangelist,” he carried practical crop education directly to farmers before returning to Michigan.
candidates.why_interesting: He helped turn agricultural science into something farmers could use beyond a college campus.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Perry Greeley Holden.
image.creator: Unknown photographer
image.attribution: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Jennie W. Erickson
candidates.short_description: Progressive educator and juvenile-court reformer.
candidates.biography: Michigan-born Jennie W. Erickson worked as a teacher and county school superintendent before becoming chief probation officer for the juvenile court in Pulaski County, Arkansas. National reform publications highlighted her programs addressing truancy, dependency, and youth detention.
candidates.why_interesting: Her Michigan roots led to nationally noticed work in education and juvenile justice.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Jennie W. Erickson.
image.creator: No photographer credited.
image.attribution: No photographer credited. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: William Comstock
candidates.short_description: Michigan governor who backed minimum wages and old-age pensions.
candidates.biography: William A. Comstock served as Michigan's governor during the depths of the Great Depression. His administration supported progressive measures that included minimum-wage protections and old-age pensions.
candidates.why_interesting: He brought an ambitious social-policy agenda to Lansing during an economic emergency.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of William Comstock.
image.creator: Bain News Service
image.attribution: Bain News Service · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Frank D. Scott
candidates.short_description: Alpena lawyer who served six terms in Congress.
candidates.biography: Frank D. Scott moved from Alpena city law offices to the Michigan Senate and then the U.S. House, where he served from 1915 through 1927. He chaired the House Committee on Merchant Marine and Fisheries during his final term.
candidates.why_interesting: An Alpena legal career grew into twelve years shaping national maritime policy.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Frank D. Scott.
image.creator: Harris & Ewing
image.attribution: Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Frederick Van Ness Bradley
candidates.short_description: Northern Michigan congressman during World War II.
candidates.biography: Frederick Van Ness Bradley represented Michigan's Eleventh Congressional District from 1939 until his death in 1947. His time in Washington spanned nearly the entire Second World War and the opening years of the postwar era.
candidates.why_interesting: He represented northern Michigan in Congress through one of the country's most consequential periods.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Frederick Van Ness Bradley.
image.creator: Harris & Ewing
image.attribution: Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Seth C. Moffatt
candidates.short_description: Traverse City prosecutor, Michigan House speaker, and congressman.
candidates.biography: Seth C. Moffatt practiced law in Traverse City, served as prosecutor for Grand Traverse and Leelanau counties, and became speaker of the Michigan House. He later represented northern Michigan in Congress until his death in 1887.
candidates.why_interesting: His career tied Traverse City's early civic institutions directly to state and federal government.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Seth C. Moffatt.
image.creator: Frontispiece of 1889's " Seth C. Moffatt, Late a Representative ". US Government Printing Office.
image.attribution: Frontispiece of 1889's " Seth C. Moffatt, Late a Representative ". US Government Printing Office. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Forest Ray Moulton
candidates.short_description: Astronomer behind an early theory of planetary formation.
candidates.biography: Forest Ray Moulton was an American astronomer known for work in celestial mechanics and for developing the planetesimal hypothesis with geologist Thomas Chrowder Chamberlin. That theory proposed that planets formed through the gradual gathering of smaller bodies.
candidates.why_interesting: His ideas helped move the scientific debate over how planetary systems form.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Forest Ray Moulton.
image.creator: (extracted by:) Jochen Burghardt
image.attribution: (extracted by:) Jochen Burghardt · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Albert J. Engel
candidates.short_description: World War I veteran and eight-term Michigan congressman.
candidates.biography: Albert J. Engel served overseas as an Army officer during World War I, worked as a county prosecutor and state senator, and represented northern Michigan in Congress from 1935 through 1951. After Washington, he returned to a large tree farm near Lake City.
candidates.why_interesting: His path ran from wartime service and small-county law to sixteen years in the U.S. House.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Albert J. Engel.
image.creator: Harris and Ewing
image.attribution: Harris and Ewing · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Gilbert Archibald Currie
candidates.short_description: Midland lawyer who became Michigan House speaker and congressman.
candidates.biography: Gilbert A. Currie built his law practice in Midland and served three terms in the Michigan House, including one as speaker. He later represented Michigan's Tenth District in Congress during the First World War.
candidates.why_interesting: He carried a Midland legal career into leadership roles in both Lansing and Washington.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Gilbert Archibald Currie.
image.creator: Bain News Service
image.attribution: Bain News Service · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Francis H. Dodds
candidates.short_description: Mount Pleasant educator, lawyer, and two-term congressman.
candidates.biography: Francis H. Dodds taught school before earning a law degree and settling in Mount Pleasant. He served as city attorney and on the school board, then represented Michigan's Eleventh District in Congress from 1909 to 1913.
candidates.why_interesting: His public life connected classrooms, local government, and Congress in central Michigan.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Francis H. Dodds.
image.creator: Harris & Ewing
image.attribution: Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Don Gross
candidates.short_description: Left-handed pitcher for Cincinnati and Pittsburgh.
candidates.biography: Don Gross attended Michigan State and spent parts of six seasons in Major League Baseball with the Cincinnati Redlegs and Pittsburgh Pirates. The left-hander appeared in 145 major-league games after his professional career was interrupted by military service.
candidates.why_interesting: A central Michigan resting place holds a pitcher whose career crossed college ball, military service, and the majors.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Don Gross.
image.creator: Unknown photographer
image.attribution: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Aaron T. Bliss
candidates.short_description: Civil War veteran, congressman, and Michigan governor.
candidates.biography: Aaron T. Bliss served in the Union Army, built a lumber and banking career in Saginaw, and represented Michigan in Congress before becoming the state's twenty-fifth governor. Bliss Township in Mid-Michigan carries his name.
candidates.why_interesting: His career joined Civil War service, Saginaw's lumber wealth, and the governor's office.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Aaron T. Bliss.
image.creator: Internet Archive Book Images
image.attribution: Internet Archive Book Images · No restrictions · Wikimedia Commons
image.source_external_id: Aaron T. Bliss, Governor of Michigan portrait.jpg

candidates.name: Gerrit J. Diekema
candidates.short_description: Holland mayor, congressman, and U.S. minister to the Netherlands.
candidates.biography: Gerrit J. Diekema practiced law in Holland, served as mayor and speaker of the Michigan House, and represented West Michigan in Congress. President Herbert Hoover later appointed him U.S. minister to the Netherlands, where he died in office.
candidates.why_interesting: His Dutch-American hometown connection eventually became a diplomatic posting in The Hague.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Gerrit J. Diekema.
image.creator: Bain News Service
image.attribution: Bain News Service · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Charles E. Belknap
candidates.short_description: Civil War soldier, Grand Rapids mayor, and congressman.
candidates.biography: Charles E. Belknap served with the Michigan infantry during the Civil War, manufactured wagons and sleighs, and held several Grand Rapids civic offices, including mayor. He later served two periods in the U.S. House and wrote about Michigan's wartime experience.
candidates.why_interesting: His story links Civil War service with the industrial and political growth of Grand Rapids.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Charles E. Belknap.
image.creator: Unknown photographer
image.attribution: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Thomas W. Ferry
candidates.short_description: Michigan senator who stood next in line to the presidency.
candidates.biography: Thomas W. Ferry represented Michigan in both houses of Congress and served as president pro tempore of the U.S. Senate. During the vice-presidential vacancy from 1875 to 1877, that position placed him next in the presidential line of succession.
candidates.why_interesting: For more than a year, a senator from Grand Haven stood one heartbeat from the presidency.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Thomas W. Ferry.
image.creator: Brady-Handy Photograph Collection (Library of Congress)
image.attribution: Brady-Handy Photograph Collection (Library of Congress) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: James C. McLaughlin
candidates.short_description: Muskegon prosecutor who served thirteen consecutive terms in Congress.
candidates.biography: James C. McLaughlin worked as Muskegon County prosecutor and on Michigan's tax commission before winning election to Congress in 1906. He served thirteen consecutive terms, remaining in the House until his death in 1932.
candidates.why_interesting: His 26 years in Washington made him one of West Michigan's most durable federal lawmakers.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of James C. McLaughlin.
image.creator: Harris & Ewing
image.attribution: Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: George Ernest Foulkes
candidates.short_description: Treasury agent, farmer, and Depression-era congressman.
candidates.biography: George Ernest Foulkes spent two decades as a U.S. Treasury field agent before moving to a farm near Hartford, Michigan. In the Democratic wave of 1932, he defeated an incumbent to represent southwest Michigan for one term in Congress.
candidates.why_interesting: His route to Washington ran through federal fieldwork and a Van Buren County farm.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of George Ernest Foulkes.
image.creator: "The News-Palladium" (Benton Harbor, Michigan).
image.attribution: "The News-Palladium" (Benton Harbor, Michigan). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: John S. Barry
candidates.short_description: Michigan's only three-term governor of the nineteenth century.
candidates.biography: John S. Barry served three nonconsecutive terms as Michigan governor during the state's early decades. He is especially remembered for bringing order to state finances after the costly internal-improvements program of the 1830s.
candidates.why_interesting: He returned to the governor's office twice and helped stabilize a young state's finances.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of John S. Barry.
image.creator: http://www.memoriallibrary.com/MI/LivIngPB/imagejsbarry.htm
image.attribution: http://www.memoriallibrary.com/MI/LivIngPB/imagejsbarry.htm · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Harry Hill Bandholtz
candidates.short_description: Army general who helped stop the looting of Hungary's national museum.
candidates.biography: Harry Hill Bandholtz was a career Army officer who served in the Philippines and rose to major general during World War I. As an American representative on the Allied mission in Hungary, he became famous for confronting Romanian troops at the Hungarian National Museum.
candidates.why_interesting: A Constantine native became an unlikely guardian of Budapest's national collection.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Harry Hill Bandholtz.
image.creator: Harris & Ewing, photographer
image.attribution: Harris & Ewing, photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Della T. Lutes
candidates.short_description: Michigan food writer whose memoir-cookbook won a National Book Award.
candidates.biography: Della T. Lutes was a writer, editor, and authority on cooking and housekeeping who drew heavily on her Michigan upbringing. Her 1936 memoir and cookbook The Country Kitchen received the National Book Award for Nonfiction.
candidates.why_interesting: She turned the food and domestic life of rural Michigan into nationally honored literature.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Della T. Lutes.
image.creator: Bain News Service, publisher
image.attribution: Bain News Service, publisher · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Albert Edson Sleeper
candidates.short_description: Michigan governor during World War I.
candidates.biography: Albert E. Sleeper served as Michigan's governor from 1917 to 1921, guiding the state through World War I and the opening of the postwar era. His administration coincided with the creation of the Michigan State Police and the early growth of the state park system.
candidates.why_interesting: Institutions Michiganders still recognize took shape while he occupied the governor's office.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Albert Edson Sleeper.
image.creator: Unknown photographer
image.attribution: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Henry McMorran
candidates.short_description: Port Huron businessman and five-term congressman.
candidates.biography: Henry McMorran built businesses in milling, grain, banking, and transportation before representing Michigan's Seventh District in Congress from 1903 through 1913. Port Huron's McMorran entertainment complex later carried his family name.
candidates.why_interesting: His commercial and political career left a name that remains visible in Port Huron.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Henry McMorran.
image.creator: Harris & Ewing
image.attribution: Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Justin Rice Whiting
candidates.short_description: St. Clair industrialist, mayor, state senator, and congressman.
candidates.biography: Justin Rice Whiting ran manufacturing and utility businesses in St. Clair, served as the city's mayor and as a Michigan senator, and won four terms in the U.S. House. He later ran unsuccessfully for governor on a fusion ticket.
candidates.why_interesting: His career shows how local industry and politics overlapped along the St. Clair River.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Justin Rice Whiting.
image.creator: Evening News Association (Detroit, MI), publisher.
image.attribution: Evening News Association (Detroit, MI), publisher. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Omar D. Conger
candidates.short_description: Lake Superior mineral explorer who served in both houses of Congress.
candidates.biography: Omar D. Conger joined Michigan's geological work in the Lake Superior copper and iron country before practicing law in Port Huron. He went on to serve in the Michigan Senate, the U.S. House, and the U.S. Senate.
candidates.why_interesting: Before Washington, he explored the mineral regions that would transform northern Michigan.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Omar D. Conger.
image.creator: Mathew Benjamin Brady / Levin Corbin Handy
image.attribution: Mathew Benjamin Brady / Levin Corbin Handy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Gail Kobe
candidates.short_description: Actress who became a prominent daytime television producer.
candidates.biography: Gail Kobe, born Gabriella Kieliszewski, worked as a film and television actress before moving behind the camera. She became a producer in daytime television, helping shape long-running serial drama for a national audience.
candidates.why_interesting: Her career made the uncommon jump from on-screen character roles to television production leadership.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Gail Kobe.
image.creator: NBC television network
image.attribution: NBC television network · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Al Dorow
candidates.short_description: Quarterback in the NFL, AFL, and Canadian Football League.
candidates.biography: Al Dorow starred at Michigan State before playing professional quarterback across the NFL, the new American Football League, and the Canadian Football League. His career included the Washington Redskins, New York Titans, Buffalo Bills, and Toronto Argonauts.
candidates.why_interesting: The Imlay City native played quarterback across three major professional leagues.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Al Dorow.
image.creator: Bowman
image.attribution: Bowman · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Jeremiah Whipple Jenks
candidates.short_description: Economist who helped bring social-science research into federal policy.
candidates.biography: Jeremiah Whipple Jenks was a Cornell economist and educator who held several federal research posts. His work on immigration, trusts, and industrial policy made him one of the early academic social scientists embedded in the U.S. government.
candidates.why_interesting: His reports helped turn academic economics into a working tool of federal policy.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Jeremiah Whipple Jenks.
image.creator: Brown Bros.
image.attribution: Brown Bros. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Bina West Miller
candidates.short_description: Businesswoman who led the Ladies of the Maccabees.
candidates.biography: Bina West Miller was a Michigan business leader who rose to national leadership in the Ladies of the Maccabees, a fraternal benefit organization that offered women insurance and financial protection. Her work joined women's organizing with the practical business of mutual aid.
candidates.why_interesting: She helped build financial security for women at a time when conventional insurance often overlooked them.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Bina West Miller.
image.creator: C. J. Peterson
image.attribution: C. J. Peterson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Agnes E. Wells
candidates.short_description: Educator, astronomer, and women's equal-rights activist.
candidates.biography: Agnes E. Wells earned a doctorate, served as dean of women at Indiana University, and taught mathematics and astronomy. She also became a national leader in the movement for women's legal and political equality.
candidates.why_interesting: Her career connected scientific education, university leadership, and the long campaign for equal rights.

image.alt_text: Historical portrait of Agnes E. Wells.
image.creator: Unknown photographer
image.attribution: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

candidates.name: Wellington R. Burt
candidates.short_description: Saginaw lumber baron remembered for a century-long spite clause.
candidates.biography: Wellington R. Burt built one of America's largest fortunes through lumber, mining, railroads, salt, and finance. His unusual will delayed most of the inheritance until 21 years after his last grandchild died, so descendants did not divide the estate until 2011.
candidates.why_interesting: Few Michigan fortunes came with an afterlife as strange as Burt's hundred-year inheritance delay.

image.alt_text: Wellington R. Burt pictured with Saginaw civic leaders in 1908.
image.creator: Unknown photographer
image.attribution: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons
